World Economic Outlook, October 2026: every indicator, for every country

Source: R/weo_full.R
weo_full.Rd

The whole of the IMF's World Economic Outlook (WEO) database of October 2026 for the 197 countries, tidy and long: one row is one country, one indicator and one year. It holds all 44 indicators the IMF publishes for countries, from 2000 to 2031: growth, prices, jobs, trade, saving, investment and the government's books.

Usage

weo_full

Format

A tibble with 238,459 rows and 7 variables:

code

chr The country's three-letter ISO code (the IMF uses KOS for Kosovo and WBG for West Bank and Gaza). It matches code in weo and wb_groups.

name

chr The country's name, as the IMF writes it, such as "Egypt, Arab Republic of".

indicator

chr The IMF's code for the indicator, such as NGDP_RPCH for real GDP growth. weo_indicators explains each code.

indicator_name

chr The indicator's full name, as the IMF writes it.

units

chr How to read the number, in plain words, such as "Percent of GDP" or "Billions of US dollars".

year

int The year, 2000 to 2031.

value

dbl The number, in the units the row names.

Source

International Monetary Fund, World Economic Outlook Database, October 2026, https://data.imf.org/en/datasets/IMF.RES:WEO, downloaded with imfweo::weo_get(year = 2026, release = "Fall"). Built by data-raw/weo_full.R from data-raw/source/weo_2026oct_imfweo.csv.gz.

Details

weo_indicators lists the 44 indicators with what each one measures. Start there to find what you can ask. weo has twelve of them already laid out as columns, which is easier for a first analysis.

A row exists only where the IMF has a value. A country and year the IMF leaves blank has no row here, where weo would show NA. So count the years a country has before you chart it.

The last years are IMF projections. For most countries the numbers are actual through 2024 or 2025; latest_actual in weo says where the fiscal data stop.

Transformations

data-raw/weo_download.R downloaded the release with the imfweo package and saved it. data-raw/weo_full.R keeps the 197 countries (the 13 IMF groups are in weo), renames the columns, writes the units in plain words from the IMF's own scale and unit, and rounds to three decimals. For the 13 indicators it shares with the IMF's workbook extract, data-raw/weo.R checks the download cell by cell: no number differs.

Credit

Print this line under every chart you make from these data:

Source: International Monetary Fund, World Economic Outlook Database, October 2026, https://data.imf.org/en/datasets/IMF.RES:WEO.

Vintage

The IMF's World Economic Outlook database of October 2026. This table is a frozen snapshot of that release: it does not change when the IMF publishes a new WEO or revises these numbers.

Examples

library(tidyverse) # load the tidyverse: dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr and more

# One row per country, indicator and year
weo_full
#> # A tibble: 238,459 × 7
#>    code  name                        indicator indicator_name units  year  value
#>    <chr> <chr>                       <chr>     <chr>          <chr> <int>  <dbl>
#>  1 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2000  0.213
#>  2 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2001  0.31 
#>  3 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2002 -0.333
#>  4 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2003 -0.167
#>  5 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2004  0.274
#>  6 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2005  0.116
#>  7 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2006  0.314
#>  8 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2007  0.259
#>  9 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2008  0.001
#> 10 ABW   Aruba, Kingdom of the Neth… BCA       Current accou… Bill…  2009  0.177
#> # ℹ 238,449 more rows

# Investment as a share of GDP in 2025: who invests the most?
weo_full |>                        # start with the long table, and then
  filter(indicator == "NID_NGDP") |> # keep one indicator, and then
  filter(year == 2025) |>          # keep one year, and then
  arrange(desc(value)) |>          # sort, largest first, and then
  select(name, units, value)       # keep the columns to read
#> # A tibble: 171 × 3
#>    name                            units          value
#>    <chr>                           <chr>          <dbl>
#>  1 Mauritania, Islamic Republic of Percent of GDP  54.9
#>  2 Bhutan                          Percent of GDP  54.4
#>  3 Algeria                         Percent of GDP  48.9
#>  4 Iran, Islamic Republic of       Percent of GDP  45.7
#>  5 Gabon                           Percent of GDP  44.9
#>  6 China, People's Republic of     Percent of GDP  38.9
#>  7 Tanzania, United Republic of    Percent of GDP  35.9
#>  8 Benin                           Percent of GDP  35.8
#>  9 Dominica                        Percent of GDP  35.7
#> 10 Maldives                        Percent of GDP  35.5
#> # ℹ 161 more rows

# Saving and investment side by side for one country: indicators up into columns
weo_full |>                                  # start with the long table, then
  filter(code == "IDN") |>                   # keep Indonesia, and then
  filter(indicator %in% c("NGSD_NGDP", "NID_NGDP")) |> # two indicators
  select(year, indicator, value) |>          # keep what the pivot needs
  pivot_wider(                               # send the indicators up:
    names_from = indicator,                  # one column per indicator
    values_from = value                      # filled from value
  )                                          # close pivot_wider()
#> # A tibble: 32 × 3
#>     year NGSD_NGDP NID_NGDP
#>    <int>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1  2000      24.9     25.1
#>  2  2001      24.7     25.3
#>  3  2002      23.4     24.2
#>  4  2003      26.7     28.1
#>  5  2004      24.0     27.4
#>  6  2005      23.6     28.6
#>  7  2006      25.8     29.0
#>  8  2007      24.4     28.7
#>  9  2008      33.0     33.0
#> 10  2009      33.0     31.2
#> # ℹ 22 more rows
